Beginners paint a ball on a stick. Show the Y fork and four round clusters.

beginner_version.found: Tiny separate things: yes, a village of houses with cypress trees, scattered bushes on the golden hill, and the balloon's ropes. Textures of hundreds of items: yes, thousands of lavender stalks. Detail inside big shapes: yes, veined, many-puffed clouds and a lake glint. Parts: about 12 at different distances (sky, clouds, sun, mountains, lake, village, middle fields, tree lines, golden hill, tree, lavender, balloon), more than the budget of 8.
beginner_version.list: Dropped: the village and its cypresses, the lake glint, the bushes on the golden hill, the ropes. Merged: the clouds into one big upper-right mass, one upper-left group, and a few streaks; the far mountains into one smooth band; the middle distance into one gold field with a dabbed tree line. Turned into marks: the lavender into rows of loose purple dabs, darker at the base, no stalks; the tree's crown into clustered dabs; the golden hill into loose strokes.
beginner_version.why: With the village gone and the lavender as dabs, every part is either a big shape or one repeated mark, and the lavender can be split into three passes.

diagrams.name: Paint the lone tree
diagrams.html:
Grow the tree from a trunk that forks into clusters

Dashed outline: what to paint in that picture. Arrows: which way to move the brush.
diagrams.noticed: The tree appears whole in one step, and where the trunk forks and how the crown is built isn't clear from the picture; beginners paint a ball on a stick.
diagrams.pieces: A short tapering trunk on the hill, then two or three Y branches, then three round clusters on top and one along the bottom, so the crown comes out lumpy and about one and a half times as wide as tall, as in the step image.

diagrams.name: Block in the lavender rows and paths
diagrams.html:
Lay out the field from one meeting point

Dashed outline: what to paint in that picture. Arrows: which way to move the brush.
diagrams.noticed: The rows and paths only look right if they all head to one point; placement depends on the perspective, and a beginner would paint parallel stripes.
diagrams.pieces: One meeting point at the top of the field about 60% across, then two wedge-shaped paths opening to the bottom edge, then the rest filled dark with the row edges aimed at the same point (a first try drew the rows as separate bands with white between them, which the step image doesn't have, so the last panel fills everything). The diagram's box is the lavender field only (the bottom 4/10 of the canvas), stretched taller so the rows are readable.

diagrams.name: Paint the striped balloon
diagrams.html:
Build the balloon from a circle and curved stripes

Dashed outline: what to paint in that picture. Arrows: which way to move the brush.
diagrams.noticed: The balloon is a shaped object that appears whole in one step, and its stripes have to curve around it; straight stripes make it look flat.
diagrams.pieces: A circle for the top tapering to a neck (an upside-down teardrop), a straight middle stripe, curved stripes hugging it like ( ), then the basket and ropes. Built the way a teacher draws a balloon, so the stripes follow the round form.

no_diagram.sky: A gradient from blue to orange to gold; the words give where each color goes.
no_diagram.clouds: Two big masses and a few streaks made by one scrubbing mark; the words give where.
no_diagram.sun: A small circle; the words give where and how big.
no_diagram.mountains: A soft band with two rounded ridges; the words give the ridge heights.
no_diagram.fields: Two flat gold areas, the hill described by where it starts and ends.
no_diagram.treelines: A row of repeated dabs, one mark.
no_diagram.lavender-dabs: One repeated dab along rows already laid out.
no_diagram.lavender-lights: One repeated light dab on the row tops.
no_diagram.highlights: Small touches on the balloon edges and the crown's sunlit side; the words say where.

summary: Three steps build a shape a beginner would have to work out: the tree's forking trunk and clustered crown, the lavender field's paths meeting at one point, and the balloon's curved stripes. The rest are fills, gradients, or one repeated mark that the words cover. While checking, the balloon step showed fewer, wider stripes than the finish, so the last step's words now say to add the edge stripes.

review.problem: The painted sky stops in a curved edge about 44% to 48% down, so white canvas shows down to 62%, unlike the sky step, the later steps, and the finish.
review.fix: Redraw with the sky from step one still covering the whole top 62% of the canvas, with a straight lower edge at 62% down and the orange-gold band below the clouds intact. Keep the clouds exactly as drawn, and leave only the bottom 38% white.

review.problem: The painted sky stops in a ragged edge about 51% to 53% down, so white canvas shows down to 62%.
review.fix: Redraw with the sky gradient covering the full top 62% of the canvas, with a straight lower edge at 62% down. Keep the clouds and the sun disk as drawn, and leave only the bottom 38% white.

review.problem: After the first redo the sky still stopped at about 55% down, leaving a wider white band than the steps around it.
review.fix: Redraw with the sky, clouds and gradient exactly as in the clouds step, reaching a straight edge at 62% down; add only the small sun disk.

review.problem: Found in the beginner check, not by a review: the balloon step has six wide stripes (red, yellow, teal, red, yellow, red), while the finish has narrower stripes with teal along both outer edges. The final step's words tell the painter to add the edge stripes, so the pictures and words agree, but the stripe pattern does change between the two images.
review.fix: Redraw the balloon with the finish's stripe order (teal at both outer edges, narrower stripes toward the sides), flat color, no shading.

Too busy for a beginner: a village, veined clouds, thousands of lavender stalks. It painted a loose, simpler version to work from.

all_decisions.label: The reference
all_decisions.think: Flatten the beginner version into shapes the lesson can be planned from.

tries.why: Kuwahara, strength 2: The clouds merge nicely, but the lavender breaks into blocky squares and the paths go ragged.
Kuwahara, strength 3: Even blockier: the lavender rows and the paths lose their shape, and the tree turns to squares.
Mean shift, strength 3: keeps the balloon's stripes, the small sun, and the path edges sharp.
